title: Der arme Junge im Grab
titleEn: The Poor Boy in the Grave
part: The Poor Boy in the Grave
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 185. Text from Wikisource (twice proofread against the original). 1857 spelling preserved (daß, gieng, Reichthum, misgünstig, Noth).
about: One of the darker tales in the collection: an orphaned shepherd boy is beaten by the greedy couple who were supposed to raise him, loses their birds to a hawk through no real fault of his own, and finally lies down to die in an open grave rather than face them again. There is no rescue and no reversal — only the couple’s belated ruin and guilt after their own house burns down. It does not soften the boy’s death or the cruelty that causes it.

sentences.t: Es war einmal ein armer Hirtenjunge, dem war Vater und Mutter gestorben, und er war von der Obrigkeit einem reichen Mann in das Haus gegeben, der sollte ihn ernähren und erziehen.
sentences.l: There was once a poor shepherd boy, to whom father and mother had died, and he had been given by the authorities into the house of a rich man, who was to feed him and bring him up.
sentences.i: There was once a poor shepherd boy whose father and mother were dead, and the authorities had put him into a rich man’s house, and the man was to feed him and bring him up.
sentences.n: dem war Vater und Mutter gestorben is a dative of the person concerned: father and mother had died on him. die Obrigkeit is the local authority, which placed orphans in households at its own discretion.

sentences.t: Der Mann aber und seine Frau hatten ein böses Herz, waren bei allem Reichthum geizig und misgünstig, und ärgerten sich wenn jemand einen Bissen von ihrem Brot in den Mund steckte.
sentences.l: But the man and his wife had a wicked heart, were miserly and grudging for all their riches, and were vexed when anyone put a morsel of their bread into his mouth.
sentences.i: But the man and his wife had hard hearts; for all their wealth they were miserly and grudging, and it vexed them if anyone put a morsel of their bread into his mouth.
sentences.n: bei allem Reichthum — for all their wealth, in spite of it. misgünstig (modern missgünstig) is grudging, unwilling that anyone else should have anything; Reichthum keeps the 1857 th-.

sentences.t: Der arme Junge mochte thun was er wollte, er erhielt wenig zu essen, aber destomehr Schläge.
sentences.l: The poor boy might do what he would — he got little to eat, but so much the more blows.
sentences.i: Whatever the poor boy did, he got little to eat and all the more blows.
sentences.n: mochte thun was er wollte is a concessive without a conjunction: do what he might. destomehr (modern desto mehr) — all the more; thun is the 1857 spelling of tun.

sentences.t: Eines Tages sollte er die Glucke mit ihren Küchlein hüten.
sentences.l: One day he was to tend the mother hen with her chicks.
sentences.n: eines Tages is a genitive of time: one day. die Glucke is a brooding hen with a clutch of chicks.

sentences.t: Sie verlief sich aber mit ihren Jungen durch einen Heckenzaun:
sentences.l: But she strayed off with her young through a hedge-fence:
sentences.i: But she strayed off with her young through a hedge:
sentences.n: sich verlaufen — to stray, wander off. The colon does the work of a dash: what follows is the consequence.

sentences.t: gleich schoß der Habicht herab und entführte sie durch die Lüfte.
sentences.l: at once the hawk shot down and carried her off through the airs.
sentences.i: at once the hawk swooped down and carried her off through the air.
sentences.n: herab schießen — to shoot down; die Lüfte is the plural of Luft, used of the open sky.

sentences.t: Der Junge schrie aus Leibeskräften „Dieb, Dieb, Spitzbub.“
sentences.l: The boy cried with all his bodily strength “thief, thief, rogue.”
sentences.i: The boy shouted with all his might, “Thief, thief, robber!”
sentences.n: aus Leibeskräften — with all the strength of one’s body. The 1857 text closes the shout with a full stop, not an exclamation mark.

sentences.t: Aber was half das? der Habicht brachte seinen Raub nicht wieder zurück.
sentences.l: But what did that help? the hawk did not bring its plunder back again.
sentences.i: But what use was that? The hawk did not bring its plunder back.
sentences.n: was half das — what good did it do; helfen takes the dative of the person helped. der Raub is both the robbery and the thing taken.

sentences.t: Der Mann hörte den Lärm, lief herbei, und als er vernahm daß seine Henne weg war, so gerieth er in Wuth und gab dem Jungen eine solche Tracht Schläge, daß er sich ein paar Tage lang nicht regen konnte.
sentences.l: The man heard the noise, came running, and when he learned that his hen was gone, he fell into a rage and gave the boy such a load of blows that he could not stir for a couple of days.
sentences.i: The man heard the noise and came running, and when he learned that his hen was gone he flew into a rage and gave the boy such a beating that he could not stir for days.
sentences.n: die Henne is simply the hen; the shared entry for henne was written for a Low German word meaning ‘thither’, a different word altogether. eine Tracht Schläge is a fixed phrase — a thrashing, literally a load of blows; in Wuth gerathen, to fly into a rage.

sentences.t: Nun mußte er die Küchlein ohne die Henne hüten, aber da war die Noth noch größer, das eine lief dahin, das andere dorthin.
sentences.l: Now he had to tend the chicks without the hen, but there the trouble was greater still: the one ran this way, the other that way.
sentences.i: Now he had to tend the chicks without the hen, and the trouble was greater still: one ran one way, another the other.
sentences.n: die Noth (1857 spelling of Not) is need, distress, trouble. das eine … das andere — the one … the other.

sentences.t: Da meinte er es klug zu machen, wenn er sie alle zusammen an eine Schnur bände, weil ihm dann der Habicht keins wegstehlen könnte.
sentences.l: Then he thought to do it cleverly if he bound them all together on a string, because then the hawk could steal none of them from him.
sentences.i: Then he thought he would do the clever thing and tie them all together on a string, since then the hawk could steal none of them from him.
sentences.n: die Schnur here is a cord, a string; the shared entry gives the other Schnur, an old word for a daughter-in-law. bände and könnte are subjunctive: this is what he supposed would follow. wegstehlen is separable.

sentences.t: Aber weit gefehlt.
sentences.l: But far missed.
sentences.i: But he was far out.
sentences.n: weit gefehlt is a fixed exclamation — far from it, nothing of the kind; it has no verb at all.

sentences.t: Nach ein paar Tagen, als er von dem Herumlaufen und vom Hunger ermüdet einschlief, kam der Raubvogel und packte eins von den Küchlein, und da die andern daran fest hiengen, so trug er sie alle mit fort, setzte sich auf einen Baum und schluckte sie hinunter.
sentences.l: A couple of days later, when he fell asleep wearied from the running about and from hunger, the bird of prey came and seized one of the chicks, and since the others hung fast to it, it carried them all off with it, settled on a tree and swallowed them down.
sentences.i: A few days later, when he fell asleep worn out with running about and with hunger, the bird of prey came and seized one of the chicks; and since the others hung fast to it, it carried them all off, settled on a tree, and swallowed them down.
sentences.n: einschlafen, mit fort tragen and hinunter schlucken are all separable, and each particle waits at the end of its clause. His one clever idea is what kills them all.

sentences.t: Der Bauer kam eben nach Haus und als er das Unglück sah, erboste er sich und schlug den Jungen so unbarmherzig, daß er mehrere Tage im Bette liegen mußte.
sentences.l: The farmer just then came home, and when he saw the disaster he grew furious and beat the boy so mercilessly that he had to lie in bed for several days.
sentences.i: The farmer had just come home, and when he saw the disaster he grew furious and beat the boy so mercilessly that he had to keep his bed for several days.
sentences.n: sich erbosen — to grow furious (from böse, angry). unbarmherzig, without mercy: the text says plainly what is done to the child, and does not soften it.

sentences.t: Als er wieder auf den Beinen war, sprach der Bauer zu ihm „du bist mir zu dumm, ich kann dich zum Hüter nicht brauchen, du sollst als Bote gehen.“
sentences.l: When he was on his legs again, the farmer spoke to him “you are too stupid for me, I cannot use you as a keeper, you shall go as a messenger.”
sentences.i: When he was on his feet again, the farmer said to him, “You are too stupid for me; I cannot use you as a herdsman, you shall go as a messenger.”
sentences.n: mir is a dative of judgment: too stupid for my purposes. der Hüter is one who watches over animals, from hüten, to tend.

sentences.t: Da schickte er ihn zum Richter, dem er einen Korb voll Trauben bringen sollte, und gab ihm noch einen Brief mit.
sentences.l: So he sent him to the judge, to whom he was to bring a basket full of grapes, and gave him a letter along as well.
sentences.i: So he sent him to the judge, to whom he was to take a basket full of grapes, and gave him a letter to carry with it.
sentences.n: mitgeben is separable: gab … mit. dem is the relative pronoun in the dative, to whom.

sentences.t: Unterwegs plagte Hunger und Durst den armen Jungen so heftig, daß er zwei von den Trauben aß.
sentences.l: On the way hunger and thirst plagued the poor boy so violently that he ate two of the grapes.
sentences.i: On the way hunger and thirst tormented the poor boy so badly that he ate two of the grapes.
sentences.n: The verb stays singular after the pair Hunger und Durst, as 1857 German often lets it. Two grapes is the whole of his crime.

sentences.t: Er brachte dem Richter den Korb, als dieser aber den Brief gelesen und die Trauben gezählt hatte, so sagte er „es fehlen zwei Stück.“
sentences.l: He brought the judge the basket, but when the latter had read the letter and counted the grapes, he said “two pieces are missing.”
sentences.i: He brought the judge the basket; but when the judge had read the letter and counted the grapes, he said, “Two are missing.”
sentences.n: dieser, ‘the latter’, points back to the last person named — the judge. gelesen here means read; the shared entry gives the older sense ‘gathered, gleaned’, which is a different use of lesen. es fehlen is impersonal: there are missing.

sentences.t: Der Junge gestand ganz ehrlich daß er, von Hunger und Durst getrieben, die fehlenden verzehrt habe.
sentences.l: The boy confessed quite honestly that he, driven by hunger and thirst, had consumed the missing ones.
sentences.i: The boy confessed quite honestly that, driven by hunger and thirst, he had eaten the missing ones.
sentences.n: habe is the subjunctive of reported speech — the confession is related, not quoted. die fehlenden is the participle used as a noun: the missing ones.

sentences.t: Der Richter schrieb einen Brief an den Bauer und verlangte noch einmal so viel Trauben.
sentences.l: The judge wrote a letter to the farmer and demanded once again as many grapes.
sentences.i: The judge wrote a letter to the farmer and demanded as many grapes again.
sentences.n: noch einmal so viel — twice as many, literally ‘once again as much’.

sentences.t: Auch diese mußte der Junge mit einem Brief hintragen.
sentences.l: These too the boy had to carry there with a letter.
sentences.i: These too the boy had to carry over, with a letter.
sentences.n: Auch diese stands first as the object, so the verb comes second and the subject after it. hintragen is separable.

sentences.t: Als ihn wieder so gewaltig hungerte und durstete, so konnte er sich nicht anders helfen, er verzehrte abermals zwei Trauben.
sentences.l: When it hungered and thirsted him so mightily again, he could not help himself otherwise: he consumed two grapes once more.
sentences.i: When hunger and thirst came over him so strongly again, he could not help himself: he ate two grapes once more.
sentences.n: hungern and dürsten are impersonal here with an accusative — literally ‘it hungered him’, the older construction. sich nicht anders helfen können: to see no other way.

sentences.t: Doch nahm er vorher den Brief aus dem Korb, legte ihn unter einen Stein und setzte sich darauf, damit der Brief nicht zusehen und ihn verrathen könnte.
sentences.l: But he took the letter out of the basket beforehand, laid it under a stone and sat himself down on it, so that the letter could not look on and betray him.
sentences.i: But first he took the letter out of the basket, laid it under a stone and sat down on it, so that the letter could not watch him and give him away.
sentences.n: The boy takes the letter for something that sees — the one comic turn in the tale, and it rests on his never having been taught what writing is. verrathen is the 1857 spelling of verraten.

sentences.t: Der Richter aber stellte ihn doch der fehlenden Stücke wegen zur Rede.
sentences.l: But the judge called him to account all the same on account of the missing pieces.
sentences.i: But the judge called him to account all the same over the missing ones.
sentences.n: zur Rede stellen — to call to account; die Rede is the noun here, and the shared entry for rede was written for the verb reden. wegen follows its genitive: der fehlenden Stücke wegen.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ sagte der Junge, „wie habt ihr das erfahren? der Brief konnte es nicht wissen, denn ich hatte ihn zuvor unter einen Stein gelegt.“
sentences.l: “Ah,” said the boy, “how did you learn that? the letter could not know it, for I had laid it under a stone beforehand.”
sentences.i: “Ah,” said the boy, “how did you find that out? The letter could not know it, for I had laid it under a stone first.”
sentences.n: ihr is the plural ‘you’ used to a person of standing: the boy speaks to the judge respectfully, where everyone else in the tale is du. erfahren — to learn, find out.

sentences.t: Der Richter mußte über die Einfalt lachen, und schickte dem Mann einen Brief, worin er ihn ermahnte den armen Jungen besser zu halten und es ihm an Speis und Trank nicht fehlen zu lassen;
sentences.l: The judge had to laugh at the simplicity, and sent the man a letter in which he admonished him to keep the poor boy better and not to let him want for food and drink;
sentences.i: The judge could not help laughing at such simplicity, and sent the man a letter charging him to keep the poor boy better and not to let him want for food and drink;
sentences.n: die Einfalt is simplicity, simple-mindedness, said here without contempt. es an etwas nicht fehlen lassen — not to let something be wanting; Speis und Trank is an old fixed pair, food and drink.

sentences.t: auch möchte er ihn lehren was Recht und Unrecht sei.
sentences.l: also he should teach him what right and wrong is.
sentences.i: and that he should also teach him what was right and what was wrong.
sentences.n: möchte and sei are subjunctives of reported speech, carrying the judge’s letter on without quotation marks.

sentences.t: „Ich will dir den Unterschied schon zeigen,“ sagte der harte Mann; „willst du aber essen, so mußt du auch arbeiten, und thust du etwas Unrechtes, so sollst du durch Schläge hinlänglich belehrt werden.“
sentences.l: “I will show you the difference well enough,” said the hard man; “but if you want to eat, then you must work too, and if you do anything wrong, then you shall be sufficiently instructed by blows.”
sentences.i: “I will show you the difference right enough,” said the hard man. “But if you want to eat, you must work as well; and if you do anything wrong, blows shall teach you all you need to know.”
sentences.n: willst du aber essen and thust du etwas Unrechtes are conditionals without wenn, with the verb standing first. He answers the judge’s letter by promising more beatings; belehrt werden, to be instructed, is said with a grim face.

sentences.t: Am folgenden Tag stellte er ihn an eine schwere Arbeit.
sentences.l: On the following day he set him to a heavy piece of work.
sentences.i: Next day he set him to a hard piece of work.
sentences.n: jemanden an eine Arbeit stellen — to set someone to a task.

sentences.t: Er sollte ein paar Bund Stroh zum Futter für die Pferde schneiden; dabei drohte der Mann, „in fünf Stunden,“ sprach er, „bin ich wieder zurück, wenn dann das Stroh nicht zu Heksel geschnitten ist, so schlage ich dich so lange bis du kein Glied mehr regen kannst.“
sentences.l: He was to cut a couple of bundles of straw for fodder for the horses; and with that the man threatened, “in five hours,” he said, “I am back again; if the straw is not then cut to chaff, I will beat you so long until you cannot stir a limb.”
sentences.i: He was to cut a couple of trusses of straw for the horses’ fodder; and the man threatened him as he went: “In five hours,” he said, “I shall be back, and if the straw is not cut into chaff by then, I will beat you till you cannot move a limb.”
sentences.n: Heksel (usually Häcksel) is chopped straw for fodder; the 1857 spelling is left as printed. Bund, a bundle or truss, stays uninflected after a numeral: ein paar Bund Stroh.

sentences.t: Der Bauer gieng mit seiner Frau dem Knecht und der Magd auf den Jahrmarkt und ließ dem Jungen nichts zurück als ein kleines Stück Brot.
sentences.l: The farmer went with his wife, the farmhand and the maid to the fair and left the boy nothing behind but a small piece of bread.
sentences.i: The farmer went off to the fair with his wife, the farmhand and the maid, and left the boy nothing but a small piece of bread.
sentences.n: The three companions are simply strung together in the dative without und — 1857 punctuation. der Jahrmarkt is the annual fair; zurück lassen is separable.

sentences.t: Der Junge stellte sich an den Strohstuhl und fieng an aus allen Leibeskräften zu arbeiten.
sentences.l: The boy placed himself at the straw-bench and began to work with all his bodily strength.
sentences.i: The boy set himself at the straw-cutter and began to work with all his might.
sentences.n: der Strohstuhl is the bench-like frame that holds the blade for chopping straw; the word is rare, and its exact sense in 1857 cannot be settled from the text alone. anfangen is separable: fieng … an.

sentences.t: Da ihm dabei heiß ward, so zog er sein Röcklein aus und warfs auf das Stroh.
sentences.l: Since it grew hot to him at it, he pulled off his little coat and threw it on the straw.
sentences.i: Since he grew hot at the work, he pulled off his jacket and threw it on the straw.
sentences.n: ihm ward heiß is impersonal with a dative: it grew hot to him. warfs = warf es; ausziehen is separable — zog … aus.

sentences.t: In der Angst nicht fertig zu werden schnitt er immer zu, und in seinem Eifer zerschnitt er unvermerkt mit dem Stroh auch sein Röcklein.
sentences.l: In the fear of not getting finished he kept cutting away, and in his eagerness he cut up, without noticing, his little coat along with the straw.
sentences.i: In his fear of not finishing he cut away without stopping, and in his eagerness he cut up his jacket along with the straw without noticing.
sentences.n: immer zu schneiden — to keep cutting on and on. unvermerkt — unnoticed, without his marking it.

sentences.t: Zu spät ward er das Unglück gewahr, das sich nicht wieder gut machen ließ.
sentences.l: Too late he became aware of the disaster, which could not be made good again.
sentences.i: Too late he saw the mishap, which could not be made good again.
sentences.n: gewahr werden takes the accusative here, to become aware of something. sich nicht gut machen lassen — not to be capable of being put right.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ rief er, „jetzt ist es aus mit mir.
sentences.l: “Ah,” he cried, “now it is over with me.
sentences.i: “Ah,” he cried, “now it is all up with me.
sentences.n: es ist aus mit jemandem — it is all over for someone.

sentences.t: Der böse Mann hat mir nicht umsonst gedroht, kommt er zurück und sieht was ich gethan habe, so schlägt er mich todt.
sentences.l: The wicked man has not threatened me for nothing; if he comes back and sees what I have done, he beats me dead.
sentences.i: The wicked man did not threaten me for nothing; if he comes back and sees what I have done, he will beat me to death.
sentences.n: kommt er zurück … is a conditional without wenn, with the verb first. todt schlagen — to beat to death; the boy is stating what he expects, not exaggerating, and the tale gives him no reason to think otherwise.

sentences.t: Lieber will ich mir selbst das Leben nehmen.“
sentences.l: Rather will I take the life from myself.”
sentences.i: I would sooner take my own life.”
sentences.n: lieber is the adverb ‘rather, sooner’ (the comparative of gern), not the adjective ‘dear’ that the shared entry gives. sich das Leben nehmen — to take one’s own life.

sentences.t: Der Junge hatte einmal gehört wie die Bäuerin sprach „unter dem Bett habe ich einen Topf mit Gift stehen.“
sentences.l: The boy had once heard how the farmer’s wife said “under the bed I have a pot of poison standing.”
sentences.i: The boy had once heard the farmer’s wife say, “Under the bed I have a pot of poison standing.”
sentences.n: hören wie … — to hear someone say something, literally ‘hear how she spoke’. einen Topf stehen haben: German gladly adds a second verb saying how a thing is kept.

sentences.t: Sie hatte es aber nur gesagt, um die Näscher zurückzuhalten, denn es war Honig darin.
sentences.l: But she had only said it in order to hold the nibblers back, for there was honey inside.
sentences.i: But she had only said it to keep the sweet-toothed off, for there was honey inside.
sentences.n: der Näscher is one who nibbles at sweet things on the sly (naschen). zurückhalten is separable, here inside a zu-infinitive: zurückzuhalten.

sentences.t: Der Junge kroch unter das Bett, holte den Topf hervor und aß ihn ganz aus.
sentences.l: The boy crept under the bed, fetched the pot out and ate it quite empty.
sentences.i: The boy crept under the bed, brought out the pot, and ate it clean out.
sentences.n: ausessen — to eat up, to empty by eating; the particle stands at the end: aß … aus.

sentences.t: „Ich weiß nicht,“ sprach er, „die Leute sagen der Tod sei bitter, mir schmeckt er süß.
sentences.l: “I do not know,” he said, “people say death is bitter; to me it tastes sweet.
sentences.i: “I do not know,” he said. “People say death is bitter; to me it tastes sweet.
sentences.n: weiß here is the verb wissen in the first person — the shared entry for weiß gives the colour ‘white’, a different word. sei is the subjunctive of reported speech: they say it is.

sentences.t: Kein Wunder daß die Bäuerin sich so oft den Tod wünscht.“
sentences.l: No wonder that the farmer’s wife so often wishes herself death.”
sentences.i: No wonder the farmer’s wife so often wishes she were dead.”
sentences.n: sich den Tod wünschen — to wish oneself dead. He takes her sighing quite literally, as he takes everything.

sentences.t: Er setzte sich auf ein Stühlchen und war gefaßt zu sterben.
sentences.l: He sat himself on a little stool and was prepared to die.
sentences.i: He sat down on a little stool and made ready to die.
sentences.n: gefaßt sein — to be prepared, braced for something.

sentences.t: Aber statt daß er schwächer werden sollte, fühlte er sich von der nahrhaften Speise gestärkt.
sentences.l: But instead of his growing weaker, he felt himself strengthened by the nourishing food.
sentences.i: But instead of growing weaker, he felt strengthened by the nourishing food.
sentences.n: statt daß — instead of the fact that; modern German would say anstatt zu with an infinitive.

sentences.t: „Es muß kein Gift gewesen sein,“ sagte er, „aber der Bauer hat einmal gesagt in seinem Kleiderkasten läge ein Fläschchen mit Fliegengift, das wird wohl das wahre Gift sein und mir den Tod bringen.“
sentences.l: “It must have been no poison,” he said, “but the farmer once said there lay a little flask of fly-poison in his clothes-chest; that will surely be the true poison and bring me death.”
sentences.i: “It cannot have been poison,” he said, “but the farmer once said there was a little flask of fly-poison in his clothes-chest; that will be the real poison, and will bring me my death.”
sentences.n: läge is subjunctive of reported speech: the farmer said it lay there. wird … sein is the future used for a supposition — that will be, I suppose.

sentences.t: Es war aber kein Fliegengift, sondern Ungarwein.
sentences.l: But it was no fly-poison, but Hungarian wine.
sentences.i: But it was not fly-poison at all: it was Hungarian wine.
sentences.n: Ungarwein, Hungarian wine, was a strong sweet wine kept for guests — which is why it is locked away in a chest.

sentences.t: Der Junge holte die Flasche heraus und trank sie aus.
sentences.l: The boy fetched the bottle out and drank it empty.
sentences.i: The boy fetched out the bottle and drank it dry.
sentences.n: austrinken — to drink up, to empty; trank … aus, with the particle at the end.

sentences.t: „Auch dieser Tod schmeckt süß,“ sagte er, doch als bald hernach der Wein anfieng ihm ins Gehirn zu steigen und ihn zu betäuben, so meinte er sein Ende nahte sich heran.
sentences.l: “This death too tastes sweet,” he said; but when soon afterwards the wine began to rise into his brain and to stupefy him, he thought his end was drawing near.
sentences.i: “This death too tastes sweet,” he said; but when soon afterwards the wine began to go to his head and dull his senses, he thought his end was coming on.
sentences.n: ins Gehirn steigen — to rise into the brain, to go to one’s head. sich heran nahen: to draw near, with heran at the end of the clause.

sentences.t: „Ich fühle daß ich sterben muß,“ sprach er, „ich will hinaus auf den Kirchhof gehen, und ein Grab suchen.“
sentences.l: “I feel that I must die,” he said, “I will go out to the churchyard and look for a grave.”
sentences.i: “I feel that I must die,” he said. “I will go out to the churchyard and look for a grave.”
sentences.n: hinaus gehen — to go out, away from where the speaker stands. He goes to the churchyard because his parents lie there.

sentences.t: Er taumelte fort, erreichte den Kirchhof und legte sich in ein frisch geöffnetes Grab.
sentences.l: He staggered away, reached the churchyard and laid himself in a freshly opened grave.
sentences.i: He staggered off, reached the churchyard, and lay down in a freshly opened grave.
sentences.n: ein frisch geöffnetes Grab is one dug ready for a burial still to come. fort taumeln is separable.

sentences.t: Die Sinne verschwanden ihm immer mehr.
sentences.l: His senses vanished from him more and more.
sentences.i: His senses left him more and more.
sentences.n: verschwanden ihm is the dative of the person who loses something: they faded from him.

sentences.t: In der Nähe stand ein Wirthshaus, wo eine Hochzeit gefeiert wurde:
sentences.l: Nearby stood an inn where a wedding was being celebrated:
sentences.i: Nearby stood an inn where a wedding was being kept:
sentences.n: Wirthshaus keeps the 1857 th- (modern Wirtshaus). Here stand really is the past of stehen, as the shared entry says — the same spelling is the noun der Stand in other tales.

sentences.t: als er die Musik hörte, däuchte er sich schon im Paradies zu sein, bis er endlich alle Besinnung verlor.
sentences.l: when he heard the music, it seemed to him that he was already in Paradise, until at last he lost all consciousness.
sentences.i: when he heard the music, he thought himself already in Paradise, until at last he lost all consciousness.
sentences.n: däuchte (of dünken) is an archaic impersonal — it seemed to him; with sich, he seemed to himself to be. die Besinnung verlieren: to lose consciousness.

sentences.t: Der arme Junge erwachte nicht wieder, die Glut des heißen Weins und der kalte Thau der Nacht nahmen ihm das Leben, und er verblieb in dem Grab, in das er sich selbst gelegt hatte.
sentences.l: The poor boy did not wake again; the heat of the hot wine and the cold dew of the night took his life from him, and he remained in the grave into which he had laid himself.
sentences.i: The poor boy never woke again; the heat of the strong wine and the cold dew of the night took his life, and he stayed in the grave he had laid himself in.
sentences.n: die Glut is the burning heat of embers, used here of the wine; heiß of wine means strong, heating. Thau is the 1857 spelling of Tau. The tale kills the child in plain words and offers no comfort for it.

sentences.t: Als der Bauer die Nachricht von dem Tod des Jungen erhielt, erschrack er und fürchtete vor das Gericht geführt zu werden:
sentences.l: When the farmer received the news of the boy’s death, he took fright and feared to be led before the court:
sentences.i: When the farmer got the news of the boy’s death, he took fright and feared being brought before the court:
sentences.n: erschrack is the 1857 spelling of erschrak, the intransitive verb, to take fright. das Gericht is the court of law — his first thought is for himself.

sentences.t: ja die Angst faßte ihn so gewaltig, daß er ohnmächtig zur Erde sank.
sentences.l: indeed the fear gripped him so mightily that he sank unconscious to the ground.
sentences.i: indeed fear gripped him so hard that he sank to the ground in a faint.
sentences.n: ja here is emphatic: indeed, in fact. sank really is the past of sinken here, and ohnmächtig means unconscious, in a swoon.

sentences.t: Die Frau, die mit einer Pfanne voll Schmalz am Herde stand, lief herzu um ihm Beistand zu leisten.
sentences.l: The wife, who was standing at the hearth with a pan full of dripping, ran up to render him aid.
sentences.i: The wife, who was standing at the hearth with a pan full of dripping, ran to help him.
sentences.n: am Herde — at the hearth, with the old dative -e; der Herd is the cooking hearth, and the shared entry has it right. Beistand leisten — to render assistance.

sentences.t: Aber das Feuer schlug in die Pfanne, ergriff das ganze Haus, und nach wenigen Stunden lag es schon in Asche.
sentences.l: But the fire struck into the pan, seized the whole house, and after a few hours it lay already in ashes.
sentences.i: But the fire caught the pan, took hold of the whole house, and within a few hours it lay in ashes.
sentences.n: in die Pfanne schlagen — of flame, to strike into something. The abandoned pan of fat is what burns the house down: the ruin comes out of their own kitchen.

sentences.t: Die Jahre, die sie noch zu leben hatten, brachten sie, von Gewissensbissen geplagt, in Armuth und Elend zu.
sentences.l: The years that they still had to live they spent, plagued by pangs of conscience, in poverty and misery.
sentences.i: The years they had left to live they passed, tormented by pangs of conscience, in poverty and misery.
sentences.n: zubringen is separable and its particle waits for the very last word: brachten … zu, spent, passed. Gewissensbisse are ‘conscience-bites’; Armuth is the 1857 spelling of Armut. The tale ends on the pair, not on the boy.

glossary.brachten: zubringen — spent, passed (3rd pl. past; separable zu at the very end: brachten … zu)
glossary.gelesen: lesen — read (past part.; den Brief gelesen), not the older sense ‘gathered’
glossary.junge: der Junge — the boy (from jung, young), not the adjective jung
glossary.jungen: der Junge — the boy (gen./dat. sg.); also die Jungen — the young, a brood (mit ihren Jungen: with her young)
glossary.leben: das Leben — life; also leben — to live (infinitive; zu leben haben: to have left to live)
glossary.lieber: lieber — rather, sooner (comparative adverb of gern)
glossary.recht: recht — right, properly (adv.); also das Recht — right, what is right
glossary.rede: die Rede — speech, talk (jemanden zur Rede stellen: to call someone to account)
glossary.tracht: die Tracht — a load; eine Tracht Schläge = a thrashing, a beating
glossary.trank: trinken — drank (3rd sg. past; austrinken: trank … aus); also der Trank — drink (Speis und Trank: food and drink)
glossary.weiß: wissen — (I) know (1st sg.; ich weiß nicht), not weiß ‘white’
